durableCommitPoint: A complete newline-terminated journal record append followed by successful journal FileHandle.sync().

interpretation.acknowledgedCommit: All baseline transactions acknowledged by the guest survived each QEMU process SIGKILL and guest reboot, with journal hash verification, immutable revision/view equality, verify() success, and stable repeated recovery.
interpretation.unacknowledgedCommit: A write cut before journal publication stayed invisible. A full journal record whose sync had returned before the cut, or whose projection completed before acknowledgment, was visible after recovery. Such outcomes are ambiguous to a caller that did not receive success and are preserved as committed journal transactions.
interpretation.kernelEio: The FUSE callback deliberately returned EIO for the journal fsync. The real guest Node syscall surfaced EIO. The complete journal record remained readable and recovery exposed the candidate; an fsync error therefore cannot be treated as proof that no commit occurred.

limitations: QEMU SIGKILL is an abrupt guest-process/VM stop, not physical power removal. The qcow2 virtual disks are hosted on macOS APFS and host caches remained powered.
The acknowledgment ledger is separately fsynced on the host and outside the guest vault, but shares the same host APFS device; it is not an independent physical witness.
The ext4 and virtio path was measured only in this Alpine/QEMU configuration. No guarantee is claimed for other filesystems, network filesystems, storage controllers, or volatile device caches.
Directory fsync errors EINVAL, ENOTSUP, and EBADF remain tolerated for platform compatibility and do not prove directory-entry durability on those paths.

The VM EIO was returned by a controlled FUSE fsync callback; it validates syscall error propagation and recovery behavior, not spontaneous hardware/controller EIO frequency or every kernel/filesystem failure mode.

The shared main worktree remains unborn; the clean S3 feature branch now shares baseline 755252c with this branch. The durability and S3 changes conflict in packages/core/vault.ts and require owner-led integration. Full power-loss durability is not established.
